title: utility allocation reconciliation customer case 01
instruction:
Marisol, I need the Wrenfield Commons water-allocation review ready for Edith Nakamura by Friday at noon. Use the supplied `Wrenfield_water_review_packet.xlsx` and return two files in the top level of the working directory, named exactly `Wrenfield_allocation_reconciliation.xlsx` and `Wrenfield_exception_memo.docx`. The workbook should give us a clean, rerunnable review of the 12 billing months and the resident lines selected for checking; keep the source material available for trace-back and show the exceptions clearly. The memo is for Edith and the Gildenhall Alliance council, so state the resulting exception rate, what population and sample it represents, the financial or operational implication, and the next action you recommend. Granthill Bureau's allocation records and the meter invoices are all in the packet, but the packet is arranged for review rather than presentation. Do not invent resident charges or silently turn rounding differences into errors. Please make the two files agree on every figure they share, identify the records supporting any exception, and include a short method note that another clerk could rerun. Ravi Ainsworth and Brigid Bonneau may need to follow the trace-back, so use plain labels and retain the source identifiers. Do not overwrite the supplied packet.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/Wrenfield_water_review_packet.xlsx` — Supplied operational packet containing the twelve master-meter invoices, Granthill Bureau allocation records, resident occupancy and move-out information, the authorized sampling basis, and the source identifiers needed to trace reviewed lines.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `Wrenfield_allocation_reconciliation.xlsx` — A presentation-ready and rerunnable reconciliation workbook containing the reviewed population, selected sample, exception classification, calculations, trace-back fields, and summary exception rate. (Write it at the top level of the working directory using exactly this filename. Preserve enough source identifiers and formulas or explicit calculation fields for a peer reviewer to reproduce the result. Do not alter the supplied reference packet.)
- `Wrenfield_exception_memo.docx` — A concise utility allocation reconciliation memo for Edith Nakamura and the Gildenhall Alliance council, with the exception rate, scope, method, findings, implication, and recommended next action. (Write it at the top level of the working directory using exactly this filename. It must agree with the workbook on all shared figures and identify the workbook or source identifiers needed to trace reviewed exceptions.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

gold.text:
Water Allocation Reconciliation
Wrenfield Commons | Decision memo for Edith Nakamura and the Gildenhall Alliance residents’ council
To
Edith Nakamura; Gildenhall Alliance residents’ council
From
Marisol Draganov, Aldbury Residential
Date
06 January 2026
Decision summary
The review found 3 substantive exceptions in 73 reviewed resident allocation lines: a sample-based exception rate of 4.1%. This is a sample result, not a census. Supporting workpaper: Wrenfield_allocation_reconciliation.xlsx.
Scope and method
The population was 7,344 Granthill Bureau resident allocation lines for the twelve master-meter billing months January–December 2025. The authorized basis uses 95% confidence, ±5 percentage-point precision, a 5% expected exception rate, and finite-population correction, producing a 73-line deterministic sample. Lines were SHA-256 ranked with the supplied seed; apartment keys were trimmed and case-folded before the occupancy join.
Source allocated charge was compared with the cents-rounded expected share: source billed invoice amount × occupied unit-days ÷ total occupied unit-days. Differences of $0.01 or less were permitted rounding. Correctly prorated move-outs were valid. A vacant unit charged more than $0.01 was substantive.
Results and trace-back
The 73 reviewed lines carried USD 122.55 of source allocated charges. All twelve allocation totals reconcile to invoice totals within authorized rounding. The substantive exceptions are vacant-unit charges, not rounding or valid move-outs. Exception List trace-back IDs: GB-2025-12-A594, GB-2025-05-A033, GB-2025-11-A166. Each row retains unit, billing month, invoice ID, and occupancy/allocation source IDs.
Implication and limitation
The evidence shows a real control failure: an occupied share was assigned to a unit recorded as vacant. It does not quantify the full-year affected dollar amount because the review is statistically sampled. Reconciled month totals can mask a misallocation between units.
Recommended next action
Do not order a full-year rebill solely from this sample. Edith Nakamura should authorize Ravi Ainsworth to have Granthill Bureau and Brigid Bonneau trace these records and run a targeted census of vacant-unit allocations for all twelve months by Friday noon. Marisol Draganov should return the census, affected-dollar total, and rebill recommendation to Edith and the council; if it confirms broader misallocations, authorize a full-year corrected rebill with resident communications.
Supporting workpaper: Wrenfield_allocation_reconciliation.xlsx. Source packet: Wrenfield_water_review_packet.xlsx.

spec.professional_context: Marisol Draganov is preparing a customer-facing utility allocation reconciliation for Wrenfield Commons, an Aldbury Residential property. Edith Nakamura must decide whether the evidence supports ordering a full-year rebill, with the Gildenhall Alliance residents' council awaiting a defensible response.
difficulty_sources: Separating the real resident allocation table from an unrelated adjacent table
Normalizing case- and whitespace-variant join keys
Avoiding false exceptions caused by floating-point representation and permitted allocation rounding
Distinguishing valid mid-month move-outs from vacant units carrying an occupied share
Sizing and documenting a deterministic sample and communicating its limitation for a full-year rebill decision
Keeping a rerunnable workbook and a concise decision memo numerically consistent

authoring_plan.source_strategy: Create one multi-sheet XLSX operational packet named Wrenfield_water_review_packet.xlsx. It is the sole factual source and should contain a review-basis sheet, twelve master-meter invoice records, Granthill Bureau allocation records for the twelve months and resident lines, occupancy/move-out records, and source notes identifying the authorized deterministic comparison and sampling rules. The packet should be realistic and text-extractable, with approximately seven thousand resident-month lines generated from 612 synthetic apartment identifiers. Do not include any real personal identifiers or addresses.

required_source_semantics.business_context: The packet is prepared for Wrenfield Commons, owned or managed by Aldbury Residential, with Granthill Bureau as the allocation vendor and Gildenhall Alliance as the residents' council. Use the supplied people names where authorship, review, or action ownership is needed: Marisol Draganov, Ravi Ainsworth, Brigid Bonneau, Ravi Fontaine, and Edith Nakamura.
required_source_semantics.review_basis: Include an authentic-looking authorized review-basis artifact that deterministically states the in-scope population, the comparison formula, the rounding tolerance, the treatment of mid-month move-outs, the definition of a substantive vacant-unit exception, the confidence/precision/expected-rate assumptions for sample sizing, and a deterministic sample-selection convention. These are genuine supplied operating instructions, not hidden authoring notes, because judgment_load is 1.
required_source_semantics.invoices: Provide twelve internally consistent master-meter invoice records with period, invoice ID, billed consumption or charge, and any rate/unit fields needed by the authorized formula.
required_source_semantics.allocations: Provide resident-month allocation rows tied to invoice IDs and apartment keys, with source allocated charge, relevant share inputs, and vendor line identifiers. Include ordinary rows, valid mid-month move-out rows whose proration would otherwise look suspicious, and vacant units carrying an occupied share that meet the supplied substantive-exception definition.
required_source_semantics.occupancy: Provide apartment-month occupancy state and move-out information sufficient to distinguish valid mid-month proration from a vacant-unit allocation error.
required_source_semantics.sample: Do not precompute the answer in a gold sheet. Make the population and supplied sampling basis determine the required sample size and selected lines. The build script must derive the expected selected identifiers and results from the packet.

exact_seeded_layout_defects: Put one unit-price or rate value in a representation with floating-point noise while keeping the source's intended economic precision explicit elsewhere in the packet. This must create a realistic risk of false inequality, not an actual contradictory fact.

Place a second unrelated table beside the main analytical table on the same worksheet. Give at least one main-table header an embedded line break in its source representation. The unrelated table must be clearly unrelated by its fields but visually adjacent.
Make some allocation and occupancy join keys differ only by case or trailing whitespace. The normalized keys must identify the intended matching records uniquely after case-folding and trimming.
authoring_plan.exclusions: Do not seed duplicate records, missing denominators, broken formulas, error literals, contradictory source facts, return rows, ambiguous classifications, extra unrelated defects, or any other standard trap. Do not include a purpose-built answer key, expected headline rate, or preselected gold output in the supplied packet.
authoring_plan.gold_derivation: Use an offline Python script with standard spreadsheet libraries to read the source packet, normalize join keys, isolate the real table from the adjacent table, apply the supplied review basis, calculate the deterministic sample, recompute expected shares, classify each sampled line, and derive every summary number. Then have an independent reviewer inspect the generated workbook and memo against the source and rubric. The reference solution should preserve source identifiers and show both copied and derived fields.

artifact_expectations.workbook: The gold workbook should contain a clean population or source-trace view, a reproducible sample view, an exception view, a monthly reconciliation summary, and a concise method/assumptions area. The exact sheet count, layout, column order, row count, and styling are deliberately left to the build agent.
artifact_expectations.memo: The gold memo should state the sample-based exception rate, numerator and denominator, twelve-month scope, sampling basis, classification treatment, representative exception identifiers, limitation, implication for a full-year rebill, and a concrete owner/timing recommendation. It must cross-reference the workbook filename.

authoring_plan.rubric_reachability: All graded facts are text-extractable from the single supplied workbook or are deterministic transformations of it. The build agent must run the derivation and a rubric walk-through offline before marking the reference solution as passed.

reference_files.purpose: Supplied operational packet containing the twelve master-meter invoices, Granthill Bureau allocation records, resident occupancy and move-out information, the authorized sampling basis, and the source identifiers needed to trace reviewed lines.
reference_files.discovery: Open the workbook and inspect the packet's review-basis, invoice, allocation, occupancy, and source-note material. The packet is the sole source of factual truth.
